**Null result worth recording rather than dressing up:** the homepage's `og:url` and `rel=canonical` both render as `https://objectstack.ai` (no trailing slash) while `sitemap.xml` lists `https://objectstack.ai/`. Next normalises the empty path on output; RFC 3986 makes the two equivalent for HTTP, so this is not a defect and I did not file it. Recording it because it looks like one at a glance and the next reader of this lane will see it too.

**Surface note:** the diff touches exactly the three declared files and only their `metadata` / `generateMetadata` objects (plus two import lines and a `Metadata` return type on the blog's, which was previously untyped — so a typo in an `openGraph` key there is now a typecheck failure rather than a silently ignored property). Nothing under `app/og/**` is touched, per the trap recorded on this card.

**ACCEPT** — PR #12325, 3 files, +155/-20, exactly the declared surface. Both open questions ruled below.

**The verification is the strongest in this epic so far.** Not a sample: every one of the **403** card URLs was derived from the *live* sitemap and fetched against production — 403/403 answered `200 image/png`, zero non-200. And the dimensions were read from the downloaded bytes with `file(1)` (docs cards 1200×630, hero 2400×1200) rather than asserted from the declared `og:image:width`.

**My assumption 4 resolved negative — and the ablation found something better than what I asked about.** I worried about an off-by-one between `generateStaticParams` and `getPageImage()` for the `/docs` empty-slug case. There is none. But the reverse-verification — mutating the marker to drop `image.png` — predicted "one 404, one wrong-card 200" and observed **two 404s**. The prediction was half wrong and the dev said so, then chased the discrepancy to the real cause: `proxy.ts` excludes dotted paths from locale rewriting, so a marker segment **without a dot** gets rewritten to `/en/og/docs/...` and the entire card surface 404s. Confirmed on the restored tree without any mutation: `/og/docs/ai/agents` → 404, `/og/docs/ai/agents/x.png` → 200. The marker's *name* is irrelevant; a final **dotted** segment is load-bearing. Filed as #12326.

That coupling is worth naming plainly: it has been latent since the OG route was written, and it only became load-bearing the moment this PR made the cards actually referenced. A rename to `card` or `og` — a natural-looking tidy — would silently 404 all 403 cards with every gate green.

## Rulings on the two open questions

**Q1 — blog OG cards: option A, keep the shared site card.** Three posts against 403 doc pages; the generator was built for the doc surface and nothing measures a pull for per-post blog cards. Option B also duplicates the OG route rather than parameterising it, which is the shape that drifts — if per-post cards are ever wanted, the honest change is to parameterise the existing route over a collection, not to clone it. No card filed: a card for a capability nobody asked for is the backlog noise this repo's scope rule exists to prevent.

**Q2 — the two `/hero-cover-dark.png` literals: option C, fold the hoist into #12242.** You are right that A alone leaves a hazard, and right not to breach the surface. #12242 re-encodes that exact asset, so it already has its hand on it; making it own the constant puts the change where the risk is. I have written that into #12242 as an explicit requirement rather than leaving it as an understanding between two reports.
